general.summary: Xpeng Inc.’s humanoid robots will cost roughly the same as an electric vehicle when they go on sale to the public in the second quarter.

Australia Firms See Inflation Holding Over 4% for Next 12 Months
general.summary: Australian businesses expect inflation will remain well above the top of the Reserve Bank’s 2-3% target band for the next 12 months, even after policymakers delivered five interest-rate hikes this year to try to rein in consumer prices.

general.title: Japan Protests New US Tariff Rate, Allegation of Excess Capacity
general.summary: Japan has protested to the US over its plans to impose a 15% levy on imports from the Asian country to address concerns over excess manufacturing capacity, a government spokesman said, even though the new level is in line with a previous tariff agreement.

general.title: Huawei Teases Next-Gen AI Memory Chip to Take On Samsung, Hynix
general.summary: Huawei Technologies Co. is preparing to release details of a new high-bandwidth memory chip that could potentially surpass current offerings from Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc., moving to launch Chinese production of a key AI component currently blocked by US sanctions.

general.title: Trump Aims to Keep Leverage Over Xi With 40% China Tariff Threat
general.summary: China has signaled it’s unlikely to retaliate against new US tariffs that remain within the bounds of a previously agreed trade deal, but the threat of higher rates shows Washington wants to maintain some leverage over Beijing.

general.title: Dry Bulk Shipping Rates Climb as Capesize Vessel Supply Tightens
general.summary: A key measure of bulk shipping rates jumped this week as exporters competed for a shrinking pool of vessels during a seasonally tighter period.

general.title: Viettel, Singtel Building Subsea Cable for Data-Hungry Vietnam
general.summary: A consortium led by Viettel Group and Singapore Telecommunications is beginning construction on a submarine cable system in Ho Chi Minh City as Vietnam’s demand for internet bandwidth rapidly grows.

general.title: China, US Must Manage AI Risks: Ex-Negotiator
general.summary: A former top negotiator for Beijing says China and the US must manage the risks stemming from competition over AI. Speaking exclusively to Bloomberg, Zhu Guangyao, who was China’s vice minister of finance from 2010 to 2018, points to artificial intelligence and industrial modernization as key drivers of development. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: SoftBank Credit Risk Tops 500 Basis Points as AI Worries Mount
general.summary: SoftBank Group Corp.’s credit risk surged above 500 basis points for the first time in about four years, raising the prospect of even higher funding costs as the company presses ahead with massive investments in artificial intelligence.

general.title: US Chip Curbs Stall Asia Data Center Financing
general.summary: US chip curbs are putting the brakes on billions of dollars in AI data center financing across Asia, with lenders reassessing deals tied to Chinese tech firms including ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent. Bloomberg’s Annabelle Droules says legal and compliance risks are weighing on banks as new rules on chip access take effect. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Microdramas Rake in $20 Billion as World Gloms On to Quick Hits
general.summary: Minutes-long microdramas are set to notch $20 billion in revenue this year as global viewers swarm to their screens in search of quick, easy hits.

general.title: SpaceX wins FCC approval to deploy 1 million orbital data center satellites
general.summary: SpaceX won approval from the FCC to put 1 million orbital data center satellites into space, a proposal that was opposed by Amazon and other groups.

general.title: Hawkish Bank of Japan Member Seeks Quick Rate Hikes on Inflation
general.summary: A hawkish member of the Bank of Japan’s policy board called for early action to keep raising the BOJ’s benchmark rate, supporting market expectations for a rate hike next month.
